- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.5), model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.  
- After a recent spike (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above recent peak.  
- If sentiment is neutral (0.00) and price has been volatile, model overreacts to short-term noise; smooth 3-day moving average before forecasting.  
- Model consistently overpredicts early in 30-day horizon when sentiment is flat; apply 1–3% downward bias for first 5–7 days.  
- If last 3–5 days show strong mean reversion (e.g., 2–3 consecutive drops), model fails to adjust; forecast should align with 10-day moving average.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.5), model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to counteract pessimism.  
- Avoid forecasting sharp reversals unless sentiment explicitly supports them (e.g., sentiment > 0.75); otherwise, assume 1–2% mean reversion.
